recent_posts.title: Design Principles Unpacked, No. 4: Balance
recent_posts.summary: Balance is a foundational design principle that creates stability and prevents visual chaos, but it has limits. When balance focuses only on reducing tension, it can flatten meaningful differences between elements — like headings vs. captions, or warnings vs. confirmations. The author proposes harmony as the next step: rather than settling elements into stillness, harmony connects them toward a shared purpose while preserving their distinct roles. Drawing on analogies from fluid dynamics and music composition, the piece argues that good design — and good teamwork — isn't about achieving equilibrium, but about composing differences intentionally so each element contributes to a larger whole.

recent_posts.title: More Realistic Tests with In-Memory Databases ASP.NET Core
recent_posts.summary: Testing ASP.NET Core APIs with in-memory SQLite and Entity Framework Core allows developers to validate real-world database behaviors without deploying an actual database. The post walks through setting up an in-memory SQLite factory and writing unit tests for common scenarios: data persistence, unique key constraints, pagination correctness, soft-delete query filters, transaction rollbacks, query refactoring safety, and DTO projections. It also introduces JustMock for mocking business rules when database behavior is not needed. Code examples are provided throughout, with a GitHub repository for reference.

recent_posts.title: Creating a Custom AI Agent with Telerik Tools 5: Creating an Interactive UI in JavaScript
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step guide to building an interactive AI agent frontend in JavaScript using the Kendo UI for jQuery AIPrompt component. Covers wrapping a custom AI backend in an ASP.NET Core WebAPI service, calling it via the Fetch API, rendering Markdown responses using markdown-it, adding a commands menu for mode switching (summarize vs. query), and displaying prompt suggestions to guide users.

recent_posts.title: Routing Management and Creating NotFound Pages in Blazor
recent_posts.summary: Blazor's route handling received significant improvements in .NET 10. The new `NotFoundPage` parameter on the `Router` component lets you specify a dedicated Razor component for 404 pages, replacing the previously broken `NotFound` render fragment. A custom `NotFoundContext` service can be registered to pass contextual headings and messages to the 404 page, enabling both generic and product-specific error messages. Combined with `NavigationManager.NotFound()` and `OnNotFound` (introduced in .NET 9), developers can trigger proper HTTP 404 responses with custom content. Additionally, .NET 10 allows inheriting from `NavLink` to write custom URL-matching logic, fixing the long-standing issue where active link highlighting was lost when navigating to child routes or URLs with query strings.

recent_posts.title: Integrating Haptic Feedback in .NET MAUI
recent_posts.summary: A practical guide to integrating haptic feedback in .NET MAUI applications using the IHapticFeedback interface. Covers the two feedback types (Click and LongPress), when to use each, and platform-specific setup — particularly the VIBRATE permission required on Android. Includes XAML button examples showing how to trigger each feedback type.

recent_posts.title: AI Crash Course: MCP Servers, Agents, AI Assistants, Skills
recent_posts.summary: A beginner-friendly breakdown of four key AI concepts: agents, AI assistants, MCP servers, and agent skills. AI agents are proactive and autonomous, capable of multi-step reasoning and tool use. AI assistants are reactive, specialized agents that collaborate with users. MCP servers provide a standardized protocol for exposing tools, resources, and prompts to AI models. Agent skills are lightweight markdown files that give agents context and step-by-step workflows without adding new capabilities — analogous to assembly instructions that guide use of existing tools.

recent_posts.title: Creating a Custom AI Agent with Telerik Tools 4: Crafting an Interactive Blazor UI
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step guide to integrating a custom RAG-enabled AI agent into a Blazor application using the Telerik AIPrompt component. Covers adding the AIPrompt component, handling user prompts, customizing output views with Markdown-to-HTML conversion, defining commands and subcommands for switching between query and summarization modes, programmatically adding output to the history view via AddOutput, and providing suggested prompts to guide users.

recent_posts.title: How AI generated contributions are straining open source maintainers
recent_posts.summary: AI-generated contributions are overwhelming open-source maintainers, creating a resource imbalance where code generation is cheap but review remains costly. Real-world cases include curl ending its bug bounty program after AI-generated security submissions dropped confirmed vulnerability rates below 5%, tldraw auto-closing all external PRs due to low-quality AI contributions, and a matplotlib incident where an autonomous AI agent published a retaliatory blog post after its PR was rejected. GitHub has responded by introducing new repository settings allowing maintainers to disable or restrict pull requests. The core problem is that volunteer-maintained projects face unsustainable review burdens, and the resilience of a project's maintenance model now matters more when evaluating long-term dependencies.

recent_posts.title: Loading UI/UX Patterns for AI Applications
recent_posts.summary: AI-driven applications introduce unpredictable response times that require deliberate loading UX design. This guide organizes loading UI patterns by wait time categories: under 1 second (subtle confirmation cues, intentional delays), 1–3 seconds (skeleton screens, indeterminate spinners), medium waits (collapsible progress panels, contextual messaging), and extended waits (percent-complete indicators, step-based progress, background task patterns). Each pattern is illustrated with Blazor and Telerik UI component implementations, covering scenarios from instant feedback to multi-agent agentic workflows. Key recommendations include replacing generic 'Loading...' text with contextual descriptions, using streaming/progressive disclosure for text generation, and providing cancel options for long-running processes.

recent_posts.title: Building Chat Applications with the .NET MAUI Chat (Conversational UI) Control
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of building a chat application using the Telerik RadChat (Conversational UI) component for .NET MAUI. Covers setting up the control, handling messages with MVVM, integrating OpenAI/Azure OpenAI via Microsoft.Extensions.AI, attaching images, and implementing IChatItemConverter and IChatAttachedFileConverter to bridge business models with Telerik UI types.
